title: Mixed precision quantization and interconnect contention sweep
content:
PURPOSE
Quick working notes and results summary for the "stepped-stress" sweep that looks at how mixed-precision quant modes interact with interconnect contention (PCIe vs NVLink) and cloud SKU driver/CUDA combinations. Goal: find stable configs for long-context workloads where quantization reduces memory but increases kernel pressure and can change tail-latency behavior under noisy multi-tenant interference.

BACKGROUND / MOTIVATION
- We've validated basic perf per-sku for fp16 and NF4 previously, but most benchmarks were single-tenant, steady-state. Real clusters see bursty host activity (GVNIC, NVMe, background ML training) and networked kv-cache access.
- Anecdotal: some H100 runs report lower p99 despite higher throughput; hypothesis is kernel selection + NVLink saturation gives different micro-queuing compared with PCIe. Quantized kernels (int8/NF4) invoke different cuBLASLt paths and have heavier shared-memory / tensor-core contention.

HYPOTHESES
1) Under NVLink-connected multi-GPU SKUs, NF4/int8 decoding amplifies NVLink transmit bursts causing transient stall/retry that shows up as p99 spikes; on PCIe-only SKUs, host-to-device DMA becomes the dominant tail cause.
2) Newer CUDA (>=12.2) picks more aggressive tensor-core kernels for NF4 which improves median but increases variance when interconnect contention is present.
3) Small-batch, long-context decode workloads suffer more from interconnect jitter because KV cache lookups trigger many small host-device transfers when prefix caching misses occur. Quantization reduces memory footprint but increases number of kernel launches per token (micro-kernel fanout).

EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN
- SKUs: AWS p4d (A100 NVLink), GCP a2-highgpu-1g (A100 PCIe), Azure ND A100 v4 (A100 NVLink), AWS h3/ecs (H100 NVLink equivalent), Google L40S preview SKU (L40S PCIe).
- CUDA/driver matrix: 11.8/515.x, 12.1/525.x, 12.2/535.x (driver micro versions varied per cloud).
- Models: 13B and 70B family (same transformer stack) compiled to three precision profiles: fp16, nf4, int8 (per-operator calibration).
- Workloads: (A) steady stream: 8-token prefix + streaming decode 512 tokens, batch=1, qps target 60; (B) bursty: 200 qps for 5s windows, idle 10s; (C) KV-warmup miss pattern: 30% prefix cache miss rate simulated to force host fetches.
- Interference injection: synthetic host DMA spike generator (random nvme writes/read), background GPU kernel burner on cohosted GPU (non-shared GPU when possible to emulate NIC/PCIe lane noise), and networked kv-service latencies injected via toxiproxy.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for per-token decode, throughput (tokens/s), host-device copy bytes/s, NVLink utilization (when available), PCIe link utilization, GPU SM utilization, kernel launch rate, cuBLASLt kernel type histogram, power (watts), GPU clocks, and number of preemptions/context switches observed via driver logs.

TOOLING / COMMANDS
- perf counters: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,clocks.gr,clocks.sm,power.draw --format=csv -l 1
- nvlink stats: nvlink --status (cloud-specific tool) + vendor telemetry where available
- kernel tracing: CUPTI sampling + eBPF for process-level io (short scripts in tools/trace/).
- workload runner: local harness with realtime tracing, logs sent to temp bucket + linear ticket for each run.
- example run cmd: python run_decode.py --model 13B --precision nf4 --cuda 12.2 --batch 1 --qps 60 --context 512 --inject dma_spike

KEY OBSERVATIONS (HIGHLIGHTS)
- Median behavior: nf4 often gives 20-35% token throughput improvement over fp16 on H100 and NVLink-connected A100s under steady-state with CUDA 12.2. On PCIe-only SKUs the median improvement is smaller (~10-15%).
- Tail behavior: Under bursty host DMA injection, p99 for nf4/int8 degrades more noticeably on PCIe SKUs (p99 multiplier x3-5 vs steady) than on NVLink SKUs (x1.8-2.6). This matches hypothesis that small host transfers over PCIe are more sensitive to DMA contention.
- CUDA/driver effect: 12.2 drivers tended to pick fewer kernel variants with larger tile sizes (aggressive tensor-core usage). That reduced median but increased sensitivity to interconnect jitter (p99 up). 11.8 had more conservative kernels with steadier p99 at cost of throughput.
- NVLink saturation: On multi-GPU NVLink skus, we saw NVLink TX bursts aligning with token-boundary KV cache refills; when NVLink approached 70-85% utilization, latency amplification and small retrials increased p99. However overall p99 remained lower than comparable PCIe runs because NVLink bandwidth > PCIe and host DMA stalls were less frequent.
- L40S behavior: L40S PCIe runs showed similar median to A100 PCIe but had larger variance in power gating and clock ramp, causing occasional micro-throttles that affected long-context decodes.

SAMPLE NUMBERS (representative run, 13B, batch=1, context=512)
- A100 NVLink (p4d), CUDA 12.2, nf4: tokens/s 740, p50 token latency 18ms, p95 34ms, p99 49ms (steady). With DMA bursts: p99 86ms.
- A100 PCIe (gcp a2), CUDA 12.2, nf4: tokens/s 650, p50 22ms, p95 46ms, p99 92ms. With DMA bursts: p99 310ms (several outliers due to host staging).
- H100 NVLink-like SKU, CUDA 12.2, int8: tokens/s 1130, p50 11ms, p95 25ms, p99 38ms. Burst injection: p99 75ms.
- L40S PCIe, CUDA 12.1, nf4: tokens/s 680, p50 20ms, p95 50ms, p99 140ms (micro-throttle events present).

RECOMMENDATIONS / ACTIONABLES
1) For production long-context workloads with mixed tenant noise, prefer NVLink-connected SKUs when using aggressive quant modes (nf4/int8). NVLink reduces PCIe DMA head-of-line sensitivity.
2) Pin CUDA/tooling matrix: until we get kernel-level fixes, recommend conservative CUDA 11.8/12.1 for latency-sensitive p99 SLOs; allow 12.2 for non-latency-critical throughput-optimized batches. Document this as a deployable runtime policy toggled per route.
3) Implement small-prefetch aggregation in host->device KV fetch path to turn many tiny transfers into coalesced transfers (reduces PCIe pressure). Sketch: 8-16 cache-key bucket prefetch window.
4) Add automatic detection of NVLink vs PCIe path and apply different kernel launch pacing heuristics. If NVLink: allow more aggressive tensor-core tiling; if PCIe: insert minimal batching and limit micro-kernel fanout.
5) Expand infra telemetry to capture NVLink/PCIe link utilization and host DMA rates on customer nodes. Expose a console flag that surfaces recent link saturation incidents tied to p99 regressions.

OPEN QUESTIONS / NEXT STEPS
- Need follow-up to confirm if driver/12.2 heuristics can be tuned via cuBLASLt env vars or if vendor changes required. Open ticket for cuBLASLt kernel selection knobs.
- Re-run with larger model family (100B) to verify scaling of kernel fanout effect.
- Test with dedicated monitoring experiments on real customer traffic pattern trace to validate prefetch threshold tuning.
- Investigate if Linux IOMMU settings or CPU governor choices materially change observed PCIe DMA interference.

APPENDIX: QUICK RUN MATRIX (ids)
- run-2025-01-10-a100nvlink-cuda12.2-nf4-burst -> logs in s3://temp-bench/mixed-quant/20250110-a100nv
- run-2025-01-12-gcpa2-pcie-cuda12.2-nf4-dma -> s3://temp-bench/mixed-quant/20250112-gcpa2
- run-2025-01-20-h100-int8-cuda12.2-burst -> s3://temp-bench/mixed-quant/20250120-h100

NOTES TO SELF
- Add quick script to correlate CUPTI kernel timestamps with nvlink telemetry; current manual step too onerous.
- Share with SRE and infra team: possible Node-level QoS for host DMA during critical windows.

REFERENCES / LINKS
- Linear ticket: RI-4823 (profiling kv cache host DMA impact)
- PR: runtime control knobs for kernel pacing: #768
- Prior related doc: "kv-cache-memory-fabric-sku-bench.json" (see serving-runtime folder)

END
